interpretation: a29 measured (50.83%) sits ABOVE per-file H_4 floor (38.47%, +12.36pp) BUT BELOW per-file h_inf_proxy (48.72%, +2.11pp). a29 is operating in the upper Shannon-permitted band. Inter-file/long-window LZ77 redundancy explains why a29 exceeds per-file H_4.

a29 measured (60.62%) EXCEEDS per-file h_inf_proxy floor (50.92%, +9.7pp). a29 already exploits inter-file/long-window LZ77 redundancy beyond what per-file Shannon estimates predict. n6-architecture has higher inter-file redundancy than anima (atlas iter_NNN.jsonl shared schema headers + papers cross-citation).

global_verdict: 80%_REACHABILITY_FALSE_PER_FILE_BYTE_CANONICAL — Per-file Shannon entropy floor (H_0..H_4) is 27-50% across both repos, all <80%. a29's measured 50.83/60.62% already operates ABOVE per-file H_4 ceiling via inter-file long-window context. Reaching 80% requires (a) corpus-spanning shared dictionary OR (b) sub-byte coding (arithmetic/range coder operating on bits) OR (c) source-level transformation reducing source H_n itself.
algorithm_class_required_for_80: cross_repo_dictionary_LZ77 — 64KB+ window over concatenated corpus (already partially used by a29; further lift bounded by cross-file h_inf which is LOWER than per-file h_inf but unmeasured here)
corpus_aware_arithmetic_coder — bit-level coding with order-3+ context (sub-byte granularity sidesteps the 8-bits/byte canonical floor)

source_transform_then_compress — schema-aware delta + tokenization (per-file H_4 must drop to ~1.6 bits/byte equivalent; achievable on highly schemaful jsonl where field names repeat 100x+ via column-oriented reordering; NOT achievable on prose .md where H_4≥4.4 bits/byte by Indo-European language structure)

unreachable_class_breakdown.text-heavy_md: H_4 mean ≈ 5.5 bits/byte (English prose Shannon limit ~4.5 + technical density + formatting overhead). 80% target requires H_n≤1.6 bits/byte — language-impossible at byte level without source transform.
unreachable_class_breakdown.json-heavy_jsonl: H_4 mean ≈ 5.6 bits/byte per-file BUT inter-file shared schema makes corpus-level h_inf much lower — observed 60-87% saving on json-heavy classes via dictionary reuse on nexus/hive/airgenome. anima/n6 json-heavy lift bounded because per-file size small (median ~5KB, dictionary amortization weak).
unreachable_class_breakdown.mixed_hexa_source: H_4 mean ≈ 4.7 bits/byte (highest compressibility per-file class due to keyword/identifier repetition). 80% requires H_n≤1.6, gap remains 3 bits/byte even at h_inf.

raw_91_honest_c3_disclosure: MEASURED: 22 representative files (anima 10 + n6-architecture 12). Total 1.80MB raw / 886KB sampled (256KB cap on >256KB files: anima/.roadmap 1.15MB, n6/atlas/atlas.signals.n6 290KB).

NOT MEASURED on this turn: full anima/n6 corpus walk (background helper terminated due to time-budget; full-corpus H_n on concatenated 30+MB takes O(N) for ctx counts but finishes 4 separate passes for h0/h3/h4 repo + per-class on each, exceeding 30min cap).

H_3/H_4 use Laplace alpha=1 PPM-style cross-entropy upper bound. True h_inf is LOWER (smoothing penalty); h_inf_proxy = min(H_0,H_1,H_3,H_4) is a CONSERVATIVE upper bound on the achievable Shannon limit per-file.

floor_pct = (1 - H_n/8)*100 is byte-canonical wire saving floor. Algorithms can EXCEED per-file floor by exploiting cross-file context (a29 already does this, evidenced by saving > floor_h_inf_proxy on n6-architecture: 60.62% > 50.92%).

Reachability verdict applies to PER-FILE byte-canonical encoding. 80% TARGET on anima/n6 requires algorithm class change beyond LZ+PPM byte coding (cross_repo_dict OR sub-byte coder OR source transform).
cmix-ban (raw 137) maintained: out-of-band heavy coders (CMIX, paq8) explicitly excluded. Verdict 80% UNREACHABLE applies WITHIN raw 137 cmix-ban Pareto envelope.

Sample-cap of 262144 bytes for atlas.signals.n6 + .roadmap may underestimate H_4 because long-range repetition not visible in 256KB window; effect is conservative (true H_4 likely lower → floor higher) but does not change verdict (gap to 80% is 30-40pp, not 5pp).

Per-file H_4 estimator BIAS: small files (<2KB) show H_4 near H_0 due to insufficient ctx samples for Laplace smoothing — visible in eeg_*.json (1.3-1.5KB sample, H_4 ≈ 6.3 vs H_0 ≈ 5.0, suggesting smoothing alpha=1 inflates bits/symbol when ctx unique counts small). Conservative upward bias on H_4 → conservative downward bias on floor — does not change verdict.
